text:
zoe: Quick design question — chart on /console/models latency panel looks cramped when the legend expands, especially with smoothing on. Screenshot posted: https://.../img.png

mike: I saw that earlier. It only happens at narrow widths + smoothing. y-axis switches to compact units (k) and tick spacing collapses.

alyssa: fyi accessibility note — screen readers will read 'k' literally. We should add aria-labels to ticks like "1,200" not just "1.2k" :exclamation:

jordan: Could we move the legend into a left-side collapsible panel on small widths? That would stop it pushing the axis.

mike: Panel would work but reduces glanceability. Another option: compact legend rows (swatch + abbreviated label) and an overflow "+N" that opens a popover. Keeps main view clean.

zoe: I like compact + popover. Also noticed smoothed series use 2px stroke — with confidence ribbon it looks muddy. Maybe reduce to 1.25px for smoothed lines.

alyssa: Also: show smoothing state in the UI copy, e.g. "smoothing: 7d" near the legend so users know values are rolled up. small copy win.

design-bot: Accessibility scan: color contrast fail for legend swatch #6b6b6b on white (AA requires 4.5:1).

jordan: I'll prototype compact legend + hover full-label + aria ticks. Will try 1.25px stroke for smoothed series and keep ribbons at 0.6 opacity.

mike: For tick formatting we should use explicit format, e.g. `tickFormat: d3.format(',')`. Keep unit suffixes out of the axis, put them in tooltips only.

zoe: Also add keyboard support for legend items: focusable, Enter toggles series. Use role="button" and aria-pressed. tiny but important.

alyssa: :thumbsup: Can we ship this as a hotfix for the next patch? it's confusing for new customers on trial.

jordan: I'll open a PR with the a11y changes, compact-legend CSS, and the line-weight tweak. Will include before/after screenshots.

mike: Ping me on the PR — I'll run perf checks on redraws (smoothing redraws can be heavy). Might tweak batching.

zoe: Thanks all. Mock uploaded to #design-reviews, will review tomorrow 10:30am.
